items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Single-letter names in the core logic (`a`, `b`, `s`, `n`, `cap`). The `#if 0` / `r""" #"` language-switching trick has no comment in the file. The only comment is `/* Big-number Fibonacci using base-1e9 limbs */`.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: All C logic is in one `main` of about 30 lines, with no `fib` helper. Python runs as top-level script code. The magic `1000000000u` appears twice. No dead code, and the test binaries were removed.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: C: `atol` doesn't validate, so non-numeric input prints 0. `calloc` result isn't checked. Missing argument returns 1 with no message. Python: no argument check, so it relies on IndexError/ValueError tracebacks, and negative n prints 0.

items.name: Boundary and large inputs
items.evidence: f(0)=0 and f(1)=1. Both are iterative, and the bignum C matches Python up to n=5000. Argument handling is partial: C prints 0 for non-numeric input, Python prints 0 for negative n, and missing arguments give no usage message in either language.

items.name: Exact invocation contract
items.evidence: Works with the exact two commands. It compiles clean even with `-Wall -Wextra` and prints only the number. `r""" #"` stays a valid token in C's skipped `#if 0` block. `set_int_max_str_digits` exists in 3.12.
